response.sql: SELECT i.invoice_number, AVG(ili.derived_total_cost / ili.derived_product_cost) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(ili.invoice_number) AS line_item_count FROM Invoices i LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number GROUP BY i.invoice_number ORDER BY line_item_count DESC, i.invoice_number LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: derived_product_cost is never zero in the data, preventing division by zero errors

alternatives.interpretation: The ratio should be the aggregate total (sum of derived_total_cost divided by sum of derived_product_cost) rather than averaging individual line item ratios, which may better represent overall invoice cost structure in an accounting context
alternatives.sql: SELECT i.invoice_number, CASE WHEN COUNT(ili.invoice_number) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(ili.derived_total_cost) / SUM(ili.derived_product_cost) END AS aggregate_ratio, COUNT(ili.invoice_number) AS line_item_count FROM Invoices i LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number GROUP BY i.invoice_number ORDER BY line_item_count DESC, i.invoice_number LIMIT 10
